description:
Sibling-pattern propagation of the design defense landed at bd:JMAP-1rwf.7.

PrincipalCalendarsCapability.account_id (crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/capability.rs:121) uses the same 'required-and-nullable' wire shape as CalendarAlert.recurrence_id — Option<Id> with no skip_serializing_if attribute, deliberately serializing as null when None. The current rustdoc says 'Required-and-nullable: always present on the wire, as null or an Id' but does NOT carry the 'do NOT add skip_serializing_if' maintainer-defense paragraph that CalendarAlert.recurrence_id now has.

The same anti-pattern hazard applies: a clippy clean-up or consistency PR could trivially propose adding skip_serializing_if, silently breaking the wire contract.

Acceptance:
  - Add the maintainer-defense paragraph to PrincipalCalendarsCapability.account_id rustdoc, naming the regression test that pins the null-serialization (grep crate for that test if one exists; if not, file a follow-up bead).
  - Cross-reference bd:JMAP-1rwf.7 as the precedent.

Out of scope: searching the workspace for OTHER required-and-nullable Option<T> fields. If a sibling crate has the same pattern, file separate beads.
title: calendars-types: extend required-and-nullable defense to PrincipalCalendarsCapability.account_id
